docs.title: qcstore
docs.text:
A store for quantum chemistry results. Every run of every calculation is kept as plain JSON you can read with cat and jq, filed under the calculation's key, and nothing is ever overwritten or deleted. Many processes can write to one store at once, on a local disk or NFS, without locks, and a writer killed mid-write leaves nothing a reader trusts.

qcstore depends only on qcdata and the Python standard library.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
python -m pip install qcstore

installs it with qcdata. To cache calculations that qccompute runs, as at the end of the next section, add the runner and its external programs:

python -m pip install qcstore "qccompute[qccodec]" qccodec

docs.title: Five minutes
docs.text:
A store files each calculation under its key, qcdata.calculation_key(inp): the input alone. Each run also keeps the numerics identity of every program that produced it, so results of different code stay apart while the key stays the same across releases. The runner sets the identities on every output it returns, execution.identities: it asks each program for a string that changes whenever its results may change, and put stores them with the run. For a Python library that is its version ({"tblite": "0.8.0"}); for an external executable, its version and the sha256 of the file ({"xtb": "6.7.1 sha256:9c1f…"}); for a program with numerics epochs, the epoch. qccompute.Runner().identities(inp) shows them for an input.

from qcdata import ProgramInput, ProgramOutput, SinglePointData, Structure
from qcstore import Store

water = Structure(
    symbols=["O", "H", "H"],
    geometry=[[0.0, 0.0, 0.0], [0.0, 1.43, 1.11], [0.0, -1.43, 1.11]],  # bohr
)
inp = ProgramInput(
    program="tblite", calctype="energy", structure=water, model={"method": "GFN2-xTB"}
)
output = ProgramOutput(
    input_data=inp,
    success=True,
    logs="SCF converged in 9 iterations\n",
    results=SinglePointData(
        provenance={"program": "tblite", "program_version": "0.8.0"}, energy=-5.07
    ),
    execution={"identities": {"tblite": "0.8.0"}},  # what the runner sets
)

store = Store("./store")
run = store.put(output, tags=["demo"], meta={"by": "readme"})

key = store.key(inp)
tblite = {"tblite": "0.8.0"}
store.get(key, tblite)             # only a run of tblite 0.8.0
store.get(key, {"tblite": "0.9.0"}) # None: never run with 0.9.0
store.get(key)                     # the latest run, whatever code made it...
store.get(key).execution.identities  # ...and which code that was
store.blob(key, "logs")            # b"SCF converged in 9 iterations\n"
store.get(key).execution.store_run # "k1:35a1.../20261117T...": read from this store

get(key) without identities returns the latest run (the latest success, else the latest failure) whatever code made it, so two builds of one program can both be behind a key. Ask with identities, get(key, identities), to get a run of that code, or read the returned output's execution.identities to see which code you got.

A new release that gives the same results need not rerun anything: carry the runs to the new identities, with the evidence. The evidence is stored once, however many runs it covers, and asserts that each run's whole output is what the new code would produce.

newer = {"tblite": "0.9.0"}
store.carry([(key, run)], newer, {"benchmark": "S22", "max_abs_diff": 0.0})
store.get(key, newer)              # the 0.8.0 run, valid for 0.9.0 too

A wrong result is withdrawn, not deleted:

store.withdraw(key, run, "wrong geometry")
store.get(key)                     # None: no other run
for r in store.runs(key):
    print(r.id, r.success, r.identities, r.withdrawn.reason)

Questions across calculations go to an optional SQLite index, kept up to date from the store's journals:

index = store.index()
index.query(tag="demo", program="tblite")
index.query(identities=newer)      # every run valid under tblite 0.9.0
index.sql(
    "SELECT formula, COUNT(DISTINCT key) AS calculations FROM runs GROUP BY formula"
)

With qccompute, a store caches calculations: qccompute.compute(inp, store=store) returns a stored result when one from the same code exists, and stores what it runs. Either way the output names its run, execution.store_run, so a result can be cited exactly and read back later, even after a newer run of the same calculation has become the preferred one:

out = qccompute.compute(inp, store=store)
cited = out.execution.store_run    # "k1:35a1.../20261117T..."
store.get(key, run=cited)          # that run, preferred or not, withdrawn or not

Two processes that miss the same key at once each compute it, and the store keeps both runs: duplicate work, never a wrong result.

docs.title: Design
docs.text: qcstore keeps every run of every calculation. This page describes the files it writes, how concurrent writers agree without locks, and what a crash can leave behind.

docs.title: Two identities
docs.text:
A stored result answers two questions, kept apart:

  • Which calculation? The input. Its key, qcdata.calculation_key(inp), is the sha256 of qcdata's canonical form of the input as given: "k1:" and 64 hex digits. It never consults a program, and it does not change when code changes, so anything holding keys (reaction networks, campaign lists, tags) stays valid across releases.
  • Which code produced the numbers? The numerics identity of each program the input names, {program: numerics}: a string that changes whenever results for an unchanged input may change. qccompute's runner asks each program and sets the result on every output it returns, execution.identities; put files the run under them and stores them with the output, and refuses an output without them. A Python library's is its version ({"tblite": "0.8.0"}), an external executable's its version and the sha256 of the file ({"xtb": "6.7.1 sha256:9c1f…"}), a program with numerics epochs its epoch, an ML potential its library's version and its model file's sha256. qcstore only compares them as strings.

A reader asks for a calculation and, optionally, for identities. get(key) returns the latest run (the latest success, else the latest failure) whatever code made it: the returned output's execution.identities says which. get(key, {"tblite": "0.9.0"}) returns only a run produced by exactly those identities, or carried to them: marked valid for them, with the evidence, after a release that changed no results for it. A carried run keeps the identities that produced it. runs(), the pointer and the index all read a run's identities from the same place, its output.

Each run also records the environment it ran in, as its output reports it (execution: host name, CPU model, GPU devices, libc version). Lookups match on identities only; a reader who needs results from one kind of device filters on the environment, in runs() or in the index.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
records/k1/<2 hex>/<64 hex>/
    current.json                    the preferred run, overall and per identity set
    tags/<tag>                      an empty file per tag on the key
    <run>/
        record.json                 meta and the output, identities included
        blobs/<path>                logs, files and large arrays, named by JSON path
        withdrawn.json              only if withdrawn: by, time, reason
        carries/<id>                an empty marker per carry of the run
carries/<id>.json                   a carry: identities, evidence, by, time
journals/<writer>/<batch>.jsonl     what each writer changed, for the index

A key k1:<64 hex> lives in records/k1/<first 2 hex>/<64 hex>/: its version and hash as directories, so no name holds a colon, which Windows forbids, and keys spread over 256 shards. Tags are lower case and never start or end with a dot or take a name Windows reserves (con, nul, com1, ...). A run id is the UTC time of the put to the microsecond and a random suffix (20261117T101500.123456Z-7c1e9a0b), so run directories sort by time.

record.json is plain, uncompressed JSON:

{
  "format": 2,
  "key": "k1:3f9a...",
  "run": "20261117T101500.123456Z-7c1e9a0b",
  "meta": {"campaign": "screen-1"},
  "blobs": {
    "output.logs": {"sha256": "e3bf..."},
    "output.results.files.orca%2Egbw": {"sha256": "06eb...", "binary": true},
    "output.results.hessian.npy": {"sha256": "56a4..."}
  },
  "output": {
    "success": true, "input_data": {...}, "results": {...},
    "execution": {"identities": {"tblite": "0.8.0"}, ...}, ...
  }
}

output is the ProgramOutput as qcdata saves it, every field written (none left out as unset, so nothing set after construction is lost), with its bulky parts moved to blobs/:

  • every logs and every files entry, at any depth (the output, each frame, the input's files, each subprogram's files, given results' files), named by its JSON path in the record. Path parts other than letters, digits, _ and - are written %XX, as in qcdata's array file names. Text is stored as UTF-8, binary files as their bytes ("binary": true), so cp blobs/output.results.files.orca%2Egbw orca.gbw gives the file back;
  • every array qcdata's save puts in its own .npy file (over 1 MiB), under the name qcdata gives it, which is again its JSON path.

Tracebacks, errors, warnings and record stay in the record. The blobs table holds every blob's sha256, checked when the blob is read back.

current.json names the preferred run, for any identities and for each identity set:

{
  "preferred": "20261117T101500.123456Z-7c1e9a0b",
  "by_identities": [
    {"identities": {"tblite": "0.8.0"}, "preferred": "20261117T101500.123456Z-7c1e9a0b"},
    {"identities": {"tblite": "0.9.0"}, "preferred": "20261118T090000.000000Z-0b1c2d3e"}
  ]
}

The preferred run among some runs is the latest success not withdrawn, else the latest run not withdrawn, else none. preferred applies the rule to every run; each entry of by_identities to the runs produced by, or carried to, that identity set. An identity set whose runs are all withdrawn has no entry. Entries are a list of identities rather than a map keyed by a digest of them: the file stays readable, a lookup compares the identities themselves, and a key has only a few identity sets.

current.json is a cache of the runs: verify --repair rebuilds it from them.

docs.title: Writing without locks
docs.text:
Every file is written atomically: to a hidden temporary file beside it, flushed, then renamed into place (to replace) or hard-linked into place (to create). Linking fails if the target exists, so of two writers creating the same file exactly one succeeds, and an immutable file cannot be overwritten by mistake. Both operations are atomic on POSIX filesystems and on NFS.

  • A run is new files in a new directory: the blobs first, then record.json. The record is the commit marker: a run without one is unfinished (still being written, or its writer died) and every reader ignores it.
  • Markers (withdrawn.json, a run's carries/<id>) and tags are created exclusively. The first withdrawal of a run stands. Untagging deletes the tag file; nothing else is ever deleted.
  • A carry is one file, carries/<id>.json at the top of the store, written first and named by the sha256 of its bytes: the new identities, the evidence, who and when. Then each run carried gets an empty marker carries/<id> and its key's pointer is updated. Carrying 1,600 runs writes one evidence file and 1,600 empty markers. A run may be carried more than once, even to the same identities; each carry is more evidence. A carry asserts that the run's whole output, record included, is what the new code would produce for its input, so a release that changes the shape of record cannot be carried.
  • current.json is the only file ever replaced. After any change to a key's runs, a writer reads the runs, computes the pointer, replaces current.json, then reads the runs again and repeats until the pointer it wrote matches them.

Concurrent misses of one key each compute. The store makes no claims on a key before a run exists: two processes that look up the same key at once both miss, both compute, and the store keeps both runs (the later success is preferred). That costs duplicate work, never a wrong result. A claim marker for work in flight may come later, with a cluster backend where duplicate work is expensive.

Why the pointer ends right: consider the last replacement of current.json, by writer W. After it, W read the runs once more and found its pointer still correct. Any change completed after that reading would have been followed by its own writer's replacement, later than W's, contradicting W's being last. So W's final reading saw every change, and the pointer is right. Two writers that read the same runs write the same bytes.

docs.title: Reading
docs.text:
get(key, identities) reads current.json, then that run's record.json, its arrays and (unless blobs=False) its logs and files. The output it returns says where it was read from: execution.store_run is "<key>/<run>". put removes that field, at any depth (a frame made from a stored output carries it too), so it is never stored. qccompute's runner sets it on an output it has just stored, too, so every output a runner returns with a store names its run.

A network or a report that quotes numbers cites the run they came from, (key, run) or the store_run string, and reads it back with get(key, run=...): that run's output, whether it is preferred or not, withdrawn or not (runs(key) says which). "The result under the current code" stays get(key, identities), and "every result" runs(key). blob(key, path) reads one blob alone. runs(key) reads every complete run with its markers.

A pointer can lag behind the runs when a writer is killed between changing them and replacing it (see below). A run it names is always complete, so a lagging pointer can only miss newer runs, which costs a recomputation and nothing worse, except in one case: it may name a run withdrawn since. Readers therefore check that the named run is not withdrawn, and if it is, or if there is no current.json yet, work the preference out from the runs.

docs.title: Crashes
docs.text:
What a writer killed at any point leaves:

killed left behind readers see before record.json an unfinished run directory nothing: the run does not exist after record.json, before current.json a complete run; the pointer lags the run in runs(); get may return the previous preferred run until the key changes again or verify --repair after withdrawing, before current.json the marker; the pointer may name the withdrawn run get sees the withdrawal and skips the run partway through a carry the carry's file, and markers on some of its runs the marked runs carried, the rest not; carrying the rest again is harmless anywhere in a journal line a partial last line the index waits for the newline

python -m qcstore verify URI checks every complete run (its record names its key and run, its output loads with every blob and array matching its sha256, its input's key is the key it is filed under, each of its carries' files matches its sha256) and every current.json. It lists unfinished runs, which are not problems. --repair rewrites missing or lagging pointers and changes nothing else.

docs.title: Journals and the index
docs.text:
The SQLite index answers questions across calculations ("how many calculations per molecule", "every result of tblite 0.8.0"). It is a cache, rebuildable from the runs, and optional: the store never needs it.

Each writer process appends to its own journal, one file per store object, so no two processes write one file. A change appends two lines: one naming the key before the change starts, {"n": 7, "op": "put", "key": ..., "run": ..., "time": ...}, and {"done": 7} after it ends, success or not. The index:

  • update() reads each journal from where it stopped, up to its last newline, and re-reads from the store every key whose change is done, replacing that key's rows. A change that started but never finished (its writer was killed) keeps its key pending, re-read on every update, so a change that completed just before the kill is still indexed.
  • rebuild() reads the journals first (so changes in flight stay pending), then every key in the store.

Rows always come from the store, never from journal lines, and a key's rows are replaced whole, so the order in which journals are read does not matter, and updating and rebuilding end with the same index.

Tables: runs (one row per run: key, run, time, program, version, calctype, method, basis, formula, success, error kind, wall time, identities, withdrawn, preferred, the whole input as JSON, and the environment: host, CPU model, devices, libc), carries (one row per run carried, with the carry's id, identities and evidence), tags and meta. JSON columns are queried with SQLite's JSON functions: json_extract(identities, '$.tblite') = '0.8.0'.

The index file lives in the store's directory by default. SQLite's locks need a local disk: for a store on NFS, keep the index on a local disk (store.index(path)).

docs.title: Backends
docs.text: The store reaches its files through a Backend: get (from an offset), put (atomic; exclusive unless replacing), append, exists, list and delete. The local backend serves local disks and NFS. Object stores fit the same interface, with put exclusive through conditional writes; their journals would be written as objects rather than appended to, which is why journals sit behind the interface too.

docs.title: Known costs
docs.text:
• A put reads every complete run of its key (to compute the pointer). Keys normally have a few runs; a key with many large runs makes its puts slower.
  • update() opens every journal file; a store written by very many processes accumulates many small journals.
  • Blob file names grow with the depth of a path and with %XX escapes; a file name over the filesystem's limit (usually 255 bytes) cannot be stored.

docs.title: append
docs.text:
append(path: str, data: bytes) -> None

Append bytes with one write to a file opened for appending.

Source code in src/qcstore/backend.py 
def append(self, path: str, data: bytes) -> None:
    """Append bytes with one write to a file opened for appending."""
    target = self._path(path)
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    fd = os.open(target, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_APPEND | os.O_CREAT, 0o644)
    try:
        written = os.write(fd, data)
        if written != len(data):  # pragma: no cover - a full disk
            raise OSError(f"Short write appending to {target}.")
    finally:
        os.close(fd)

def list(self, path: str) -> list[str]:
    """The visible names directly inside a directory, sorted."""
    try:
        names = os.listdir(self._path(path))
    except (FileNotFoundError, NotADirectoryError):
        return []
    return sorted(n for n in names if not n.startswith("."))

docs.text:
put(
    path: str, data: bytes, *, replace: bool = False
) -> None

Write a file atomically: a flushed temporary file, renamed or linked in.

Source code in src/qcstore/backend.py 
def put(self, path: str, data: bytes, *, replace: bool = False) -> None:
    """Write a file atomically: a flushed temporary file, renamed or linked in."""
    target = self._path(path)
    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    temporary = target.with_name(f".{target.name}.{secrets.token_hex(4)}.tmp")
    with temporary.open("xb") as f:
        f.write(data)
        f.flush()
        os.fsync(f.fileno())
    try:
        if replace:
            os.replace(temporary, target)
        else:
            os.link(temporary, target)
    finally:
        temporary.unlink(missing_ok=True)

docs.title: Index
docs.text:
An optional SQLite index of a store, for questions across calculations.

The index is a cache: the store's files are the truth, and Index.rebuild remakes the index from them. Index.update instead reads the journal lines it has not seen and re-reads from the store every key they name, so updating and rebuilding end with the same index (a journal line only says which key changed; the rows always come from the store).

Tables:

  • runs: one row per run: key, run, time (UTC, ISO 8601), program, version (as the output reports it), calctype, method, basis, formula, success, error_kind, wall_time (s), identities (JSON), withdrawn, preferred (the run Store.get returns without identities), input (the input as JSON, files left out), and the environment it ran in, as its output reports it: host, cpu_model, devices (JSON list) and libc.
  • carries: key, run, carry (its id), identities (JSON), evidence (JSON), time: one row per run carried.
  • tags: key, tag.
  • meta: key, run, name, value (strings and numbers as they are; lists and objects as JSON).

Query JSON columns with SQLite's JSON functions: json_extract(identities, '$.tblite') = '0.8.0', json_extract(input, '$.keywords.maxiter').

docs.title: qcstore.Index
docs.text:
Index(store: Store, path: Path)

A store's SQLite index; Store.index opens one, up to date.

Each method opens its own connection, so an index may be used from several threads and processes at once (on a local disk: SQLite's locks need one).

Attributes:

Name Type Description store

The store indexed.

path

The SQLite file.

Source code in src/qcstore/index.py 
def __init__(self, store: Store, path: Path) -> None:
    """Open the index file, creating or rebuilding it if needed, and update it."""
    self.store = store
    self.path = path
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    with self._writing() as db:
        fresh = db.execute("PRAGMA user_version").fetchone()[0] != SCHEMA
        if fresh:
            tables = db.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'")
            for (name,) in tables.fetchall():
                db.execute(f"DROP TABLE {name}")
            for statement in _TABLES:
                db.execute(statement)
            db.execute(f"PRAGMA user_version = {SCHEMA}")
    if fresh:
        self.rebuild()
    else:
        self.update()

def query(
    self,
    *,
    tag: str | None = None,
    identities: Mapping[str, str] | None = None,
    **columns: Any,
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Runs whose columns equal the values given, oldest first within each key.

    Args:
        tag: Only calculations with this tag.
        identities: Only runs valid under these numerics, produced by them or
            carried to them: ``{"tblite": "0.8.0"}`` matches every run whose
            tblite numerics is 0.8.0, whatever its other programs'.
        **columns: Values of the ``runs`` columns (``program="xtb"``,
            ``success=True``, ``preferred=True``); None matches NULL.

    Returns:
        One dict per run, with ``identities``, ``input`` and ``devices`` parsed
        from JSON.

    Raises:
        ValueError: An unknown column, or a program name holding ``"``.
    """
    where: list[str] = []
    params: list[Any] = []
    for name, value in columns.items():
        if name not in _COLUMNS:
            raise ValueError(f"No column {name!r}; the columns are {_COLUMNS}.")
        where.append(f"{name} IS ?")
        params.append(value)
    if tag is not None:
        where.append("key IN (SELECT key FROM tags WHERE tag = ?)")
        params.append(tag)
    if identities:
        paths = []
        for program, numerics in identities.items():
            if '"' in program:
                raise ValueError(f"Not a program name: {program!r}.")
            paths += [f'$."{program}"', numerics]
        match = " AND ".join(
            ["json_extract({0}.identities, ?) = ?"] * len(identities)
        )
        where.append(
            f"(({match.format('runs')}) OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM carries WHERE "
            f"carries.key = runs.key AND carries.run = runs.run AND "
            f"{match.format('carries')}))"
        )
        params += paths + paths
    text = "SELECT * FROM runs"
    if where:
        text += " WHERE " + " AND ".join(where)
    rows = self.sql(text + " ORDER BY key, run", params)
    for row in rows:
        for name in _BOOLEAN:
            row[name] = bool(row[name])
        for name in ("identities", "input", "devices"):
            row[name] = json.loads(row[name])
    return rows

def rebuild(self) -> None:
    """Remake the index from every run in the store."""
    with self._writing() as db:
        for table in (*_STORE_TABLES, "journals", "pending"):
            db.execute(f"DELETE FROM {table}")
        # Journals first: a change still running is pending, so the next update
        # re-reads its key even if this scan saw the key before it finished.
        offsets: dict[str, int] = {}
        pending: dict[tuple[str, int], str] = {}
        self._read_journals(offsets, pending)
        for key in self.store._keys():
            self._refresh(db, key)
        self._save_journals(db, offsets, pending)

def sql(
    self, text: str, params: Sequence[Any] | Mapping[str, Any] = ()
) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Run a read-only SQL query; return one dict per row, by column name.

    Example:
        How many calculations per molecule:

        ```python
        index.sql(
            "SELECT formula, COUNT(DISTINCT key) AS n FROM runs "
            "GROUP BY formula ORDER BY n DESC"
        )
        ```
    """
    uri = self.path.absolute().as_uri() + "?mode=ro"
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(uri, uri=True, timeout=60)) as db:
        cursor = db.execute(text, params)
        names = [d[0] for d in cursor.description or ()]
        return [dict(zip(names, row, strict=True)) for row in cursor.fetchall()]

def update(self) -> None:
    """Bring the index up to date: re-read every key the new journal lines name."""
    with self._writing() as db:
        offsets: dict[str, int] = dict(
            db.execute("SELECT path, offset FROM journals")
        )
        pending = {(p, n): k for p, n, k in db.execute("SELECT * FROM pending")}
        done = self._read_journals(offsets, pending)
        for key in sorted(done | set(pending.values())):
            self._refresh(db, key)
        self._save_journals(db, offsets, pending)

def __init__(self, uri: str | os.PathLike[str] | Backend) -> None:
    """Open a store.

    Args:
        uri: A directory (a path or a ``file://`` URI), local or on NFS, made on the
            first write; or a `Backend`.

    Raises:
        ValueError: A URI scheme without a backend.
    """
    if isinstance(uri, str | os.PathLike):
        text = os.fspath(uri)
        if "://" in text:
            parsed = urlparse(text)
            if parsed.scheme != "file":
                raise ValueError(f"No qcstore backend for {parsed.scheme}:// URIs.")
            text = unquote(parsed.path)
        self.backend: Backend = LocalBackend(text)
    else:
        self.backend = uri
    self._journal = _Journal(self.backend)

def carry(
    self,
    runs: Iterable[tuple[str, str]],
    identities: Identities,
    evidence: Mapping[str, Any],
) -> str:
    """Declare runs valid for other identities too, citing the evidence once.

    A carry asserts that each run's whole output, ``record`` included, is what the
    code of the new identities would produce for its input, within the
    calculation's accuracy. Carry after a release that changes no results, with
    evidence that it does not (a benchmark rerun); a release that changes the shape
    of ``record`` cannot be carried. Lookups under the new identities then reuse
    the runs. Nothing is copied: the carry is one file, ``carries/<id>.json``, and
    each run gets an empty marker naming it.

    Args:
        runs: ``(key, run)`` pairs: from `runs`, `iter`, or an index query.
        identities: The identities the runs are also valid for.
        evidence: JSON: what was compared, and how closely it agreed.

    Returns:
        The carry's id: the sha256 of its file.

    Raises:
        KeyError: A run that is not in the store; nothing is carried then.
        ValueError: No runs, or ``evidence`` is not JSON.
        TypeError: ``identities`` are not strings to strings.
    """
    identities = dict(sorted(_check_strings(identities).items()))
    by_key: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for key, run in runs:
        by_key.setdefault(key, []).append(self._run_id(key, run))
    if not by_key:
        raise ValueError("Name at least one (key, run) to carry.")
    document = _dumps(
        {
            "identities": identities,
            "evidence": _json_object(evidence, "evidence"),
            "by": _user(),
            "time": _now(),
        }
    )
    carry = _digest(document)
    _put_once(self.backend, f"carries/{carry}.json", document)
    for key, key_runs in by_key.items():
        with self._journal.op("carry", key, runs=key_runs, carry=carry):
            for run in dict.fromkeys(key_runs):
                _put_once(
                    self.backend, f"{_run_dir(key, run)}/carries/{carry}", b""
                )
            self._update_pointer(key)
    return carry

def copy_to(self, other: Store, keys: Iterable[str] | None = None) -> int:
    """Copy runs into another store, unchanged: ids, times and contents.

    Runs the other store has are skipped, but their withdrawals and carries are
    copied, as are the keys' tags, so the other store prefers the same runs.

    Args:
        other: The destination.
        keys: The calculations to copy; None for all.

    Returns:
        The number of runs copied.
    """
    copied = 0
    for key in self.iter() if keys is None else keys:
        runs = self._run_ids(_check_key(key))
        if not runs:
            continue
        tags = self.backend.list(f"{_key_dir(key)}/tags")
        with other._journal.op("copy", key, runs=runs, tags=tags):
            for run in runs:
                copied += other._copy_run(self.backend, key, run)
            for tag in tags:
                _put_once(other.backend, f"{_key_dir(key)}/tags/{tag}", b"")
            other._update_pointer(key)
    return copied

def get(
    self,
    key: str,
    identities: Identities | None = None,
    *,
    run: str | None = None,
    blobs: bool = True,
) -> Output | None:
    """Return the preferred run's output, or one named run's; None if there is none.

    The preferred run is the latest success not withdrawn, else the latest run not
    withdrawn. Without ``identities`` that is the latest run whatever code made
    it: the returned output's ``execution.identities`` says which. With
    ``identities``, only runs produced by exactly those identities, or carried to
    them, count. A carried run keeps the identities that produced it.

    With ``run``, that run is returned whether it is preferred or not, withdrawn
    or not: a citation of a run (an output's ``execution.store_run``) reads back
    exactly what was cited. `runs` says whether it was withdrawn.

    Args:
        key: The calculation's key.
        identities: The numerics identity of each program the input names, as the
            caller would run them now; None for any.
        run: A run of the key: its id, or ``"<key>/<run>"`` as in
            ``execution.store_run``. Not with ``identities``.
        blobs: Load logs and files. False leaves them out (``logs`` None, ``files``
            empty) and reads only the record and its arrays.

    Returns:
        The output as stored, with ``execution.store_run`` set to ``"<key>/<run>"``:
        where it was read from. None if there is none (or no such run).

    Raises:
        ValueError: ``key`` is not a key; ``run`` is not a run id, or names
            another key; or both ``run`` and ``identities`` are given.
    """
    _check_key(key)
    if run is None:
        run = self._preferred(key, identities)
    else:
        if identities is not None:
            raise ValueError("Pass identities or a run, not both.")
        run = _check_run(key, run)
        if not self.backend.exists(f"{_run_dir(key, run)}/record.json"):
            return None
    return None if run is None else self._load(key, run, blobs)

def index(self, path: str | os.PathLike[str] | None = None) -> Index:
    """Open the store's SQLite index, brought up to date from the journals.

        path = self.backend.root / "index.sqlite"

def put(
    self,
    output: Output,
    *,
    tags: Iterable[str] = (),
    meta: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> str:
    """Add a run under the key of ``output.input_data``.

    The run is filed under the identities of the code that produced it,
    ``output.execution.identities`` (``{program: numerics}``), which the runner
    sets on every output, and is found again under exactly these. They are stored
    with the output. ``execution.store_run`` says where an output was read from,
    so it is never stored, at any depth.

    Args:
        output: The calculation's output, successful or not, with its identities.
        tags: Tags for the key.
        meta: JSON metadata stored with the run.

    Returns:
        The new run's id.

    Raises:
        ValueError: ``output`` has no identities; or it is a session frame
            (``record.warm_start`` true): a warm start can reach another solution
            than the input alone, so it is not that input's result. Or a tag is
            invalid, or ``meta`` is not JSON.
    """
    if not output.execution.identities:
        raise ValueError(
            "This output does not say which code produced it: "
            "output.execution.identities is empty. qccompute's runner sets it; "
            "a store keeps only results whose code it can name."
        )
    if output.record.get("warm_start") is True:
        raise ValueError(
            "This output started warm from a session's history (record.warm_start "
            "is true), so it may not be the result of its input alone; a store "
            "keeps only calculations run from their input."
        )
    inp = output.input_data
    key = self.key(inp)
    tags = _check_tags(tags)
    meta = _json_object(meta or {}, "meta")
    run = _new_run_id()
    files = _run_files(key, run, output, meta)
    with self._journal.op("put", key, run=run, tags=tags):
        self._write_run(key, run, files)
        for tag in tags:
            _put_once(self.backend, f"{_key_dir(key)}/tags/{tag}", b"")
        self._update_pointer(key)
    return run

def verify(store: Store, *, repair: bool = False) -> Report:
    """Check every run of every calculation in a store.

    For each complete run: its record names its key and run, its output loads (every
    blob and array file matching its sha256), the key recomputed from its input is the
    key it is filed under, its output names its identities, and each of its carries'
    files matches its sha256. For each
    key: ``current.json`` names the runs the rules prefer.

    Args:
        store: The store.
        repair: Rewrite each ``current.json`` that is missing or wrong (a writer died
            between storing a run and updating the pointer). Nothing else is changed.

    Returns:
        The report.
    """
    report = Report()
    strays: list[str] = []
    for key in store._keys(strays):
        report.keys += 1
        directory = _key_dir(key)
        for name in store.backend.list(directory):
            if _RUN.fullmatch(name) and not store.backend.exists(
                f"{directory}/{name}/record.json"
            ):
                report.incomplete.append(f"{directory}/{name}")
        try:
            runs = store._read_runs(key)
        except Exception as e:
            report.problems.append(f"{directory}: unreadable: {e}")
            continue
        for run in runs:
            report.runs += 1
            where = _run_dir(key, run.id)
            try:
                if (run.record["key"], run.record["run"]) != (key, run.id):
                    raise ValueError(
                        f"the record names {run.record['key']} {run.record['run']}"
                    )
                output = store._load(key, run.id, blobs=True)
                if store.key(output.input_data) != key:
                    raise ValueError("its input's key is not the key it is filed under")
                if not output.execution.identities:
                    raise ValueError("its output has no identities")
            except Exception as e:
                report.problems.append(f"{where}: {e}")
        if not runs:
            continue
        stored = store._pointer_now(key)
        if stored != _pointer(runs):
            if repair:
                store._update_pointer(key)
                report.repaired.append(f"{directory}/current.json")
            else:
                state = "missing" if stored is None else "stale"
                report.problems.append(
                    f"{directory}/current.json: {state}; `verify --repair` rewrites it"
                )
    report.problems += [
        f"{path}: not part of the layout (records/k1/<2 hex>/<64 hex>)"
        for path in strays
    ]
    return report
